content.text: {"label":"unknown_demand_surge","explanation":"Both queues have run well above forecast all day: payments +22% and general +32% so far, and +19% to +54% in every interval since 14:30. The excess is spread across almost every call reason rather than one dominant issue. The largest excesses are payment_status_enquiry (1.57x) on payments and login_issue (1.62x) on general, but every other reason except refund_status and other_payments on payments is also up 1.2x to 1.5x. Nothing in the data explains the surge. The two open incidents are internal P4s with no customer impact, there are no marketing calendar entries, and absences (2 per queue) are at or below normal. AHT is roughly on forecast. Service level recovered to 95-100% from 15:15 because staffing rose. However, the 15:30 overtime and the 16:00 chat deflection have both ended, and volume is still about 30-40% over forecast. So this is a demand surge of unknown cause.","plan_name":"Sustain recovery through close: extend deflection, callback safety net, small overtime top-up","rationale":"The surge is persisting while the earlier levers have expired, so service level is at risk for the rest of the day. Chat deflection worked during the day and is cheap. Each queue sees about 120-150 eligible calls per hour, so at 20% this is roughly 25-30 chats per hour per queue, about Rs 1,300-1,500 per hour across both queues. IVR callback is free and only triggers when waits exceed 120 s, so it acts as a safety net that smooths peaks without hurting service level while it is healthy. Breaks scheduled 16:00-17:30 can be pushed back for agents not already delayed today, at no cost. Overtime already offered today (40 offers, about 16 accepted for 2 h each) has used roughly Rs 11,500 of the Rs 15,000 budget. A small top-up of 4 offers per queue for 16:30-18:30 should yield about 3-4 agents, costing about Rs 2,200-2,900 and staying within budget.
